steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write a short introduction for our paper on using Value Sensitive Design to guide Responsible AI toolkits. Motivate RAI toolkits and VSD, state the two research questions, describe the workshop study briefly, and list our contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. RAI toolkits, RAI values, and VSD as a guiding framework
2. Research questions
3. Workshop study
4. Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Background
- risks of AI systems -> surge of toolkits for practical design of Responsible AI (RAI)
- RAI: responsible design, development, use; values like fairness, transparency
- Value Sensitive Design (VSD): similar objectives, recognised for more human-centred AI
- hypothesis: VSD can guide creation of RAI toolkits (human values in design process)
- unclear: alignment of VSD and RAI values; how toolkits incorporate VSD
- two aspects for supporting VSD: a) stakeholder inclusion + collaboration to elicit values; b) educating toolkit users -> self-reflexivity, responsible decision-making

2. RQs
- RQ 1: alignment of VSD values with RAI values
- RQ 2: how RAI toolkits incorporate VSD, support collaboration and learning

3. Study
- workshops, 17 participants (AI researchers) (§ 3)
- expression of VSD values within RAI toolkits; design features vs perceptions of stakeholder collaboration and learning

4. Contributions
- (i) mapping VSD values onto common RAI values in toolkits; high alignment, consensus among participants (§ 4.1)
- (ii) links between toolkit design features and promoting VSD: navigation -> iteration; open-ended cuing -> collaboration vs solo work; examples/case studies -> learning; value incorporation -> lower cognitive load (§ 4.1)
- (iii) six practical design recommendations for value sensitivity (§ 5); concrete features like actionability, shared knowledge; complement broader suggestions on focuses/approaches of RAI toolkits

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
The risks associated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems have increased, and this has led to a surge in developing toolkits that aim to help with the practical design of Responsible AI (RAI). RAI argues for designing, developing, and using AI systems responsibly, in line with values like fairness and transparency. Value Sensitive Design (VSD) is a framework that has similar objectives, and it is recognised for creating AI systems that are more human-centred. In this study we hypothesise that VSD can guide the creation of RAI toolkits effectively, because it considers human values in the process of designing technology. However, it is not clear how much VSD and RAI values align, and how existing RAI toolkits incorporate VSD. There are two critical aspects for supporting VSD: a) making it possible to include stakeholders and collaborate with them so that their values can be elicited and understood, and b) helping educate the users of the toolkits so that self-reflexivity and responsible decision-making are promoted.

This paper focuses on how VSD can be applied in practice in RAI toolkits, with two Research Questions (RQs):

- • RQ 1: How closely do Value Sensitive Design (VSD) values align with Responsible AI (RAI) values?

- • RQ 2: How do existing RAI toolkits incorporate VSD, and support collaboration and learning?

3. Study (to write)
- workshops, 17 participants (AI researchers) (§ 3)
- VSD values within RAI toolkits; design features vs perceived stakeholder collaboration and learning

4. Contributions (to write)
- (i) VSD values mapped onto common RAI values; high alignment, participant consensus (§ 4.1)
- (ii) design features -> VSD: navigation/iteration, open-ended cuing/collaboration vs solo work, examples + case studies/learning, value incorporation/cognitive load (§ 4.1)
- (iii) six practical design recommendations (§ 5): actionability, shared knowledge; complement broader suggestions for RAI toolkits

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
The risks associated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems have increased, and this has led to a surge in developing toolkits that aim to help with the practical design of Responsible AI (RAI). RAI argues for designing, developing, and using AI systems responsibly, in line with values like fairness and transparency. Value Sensitive Design (VSD) is a framework that has similar objectives, and it is recognised for creating AI systems that are more human-centred. In this study we hypothesise that VSD can guide the creation of RAI toolkits effectively, because it considers human values in the process of designing technology. However, it is not clear how much VSD and RAI values align, and how existing RAI toolkits incorporate VSD. There are two critical aspects for supporting VSD: a) making it possible to include stakeholders and collaborate with them so that their values can be elicited and understood, and b) helping educate the users of the toolkits so that self-reflexivity and responsible decision-making are promoted.

This paper focuses on how VSD can be applied in practice in RAI toolkits, with two Research Questions (RQs):

- • RQ 1: How closely do Value Sensitive Design (VSD) values align with Responsible AI (RAI) values?

- • RQ 2: How do existing RAI toolkits incorporate VSD, and support collaboration and learning?

To answer these questions, we did an empirical investigation with workshops with 17 participants (AI researchers) (§ 3). The workshops were about how VSD values are expressed within RAI toolkits, and how the design features of the toolkits affect how participants perceive stakeholder collaboration and learning.

The study has three contributions. (i) We map VSD values onto RAI values that are commonly integrated into the toolkits, and we find a high degree of alignment between the two sets of values, shown by consensus among the workshop participants (§ 4.1). (ii) We identify key links between design features in RAI toolkits and how they help promote VSD. These were: navigation methods that support iteration, open-ended cuing that supports collaboration versus solo work, examples and case studies that give learning opportunities, and value incorporation that reduces cognitive load (§ 4.1). (iii) We formulate six practical design recommendations to improve value sensitivity in RAI toolkits (§ 5). These recommendations focus on concrete design features like supporting actionability and shared knowledge, and they complement recent broader suggestions about the focuses and approaches of RAI toolkits.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
The increasing risks associated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems [1,2] have led to a surge in the development of toolkits aimed at facilitating the practical design of Responsible AI (RAI) [3]. RAI advocates for the responsible design, development, and use of AI systems, in line with values like fairness and transparency [4]. Value Sensitive Design (VSD) is a framework with similar objectives, recognised for creating more human-centred AI systems [5]. This study hypothesises that VSD can effectively guide the creation of RAI toolkits, given its consideration of human values in the technology design process. However, the extent of alignment between VSD and RAI values, and how existing RAI toolkits incorporate VSD, remain unclear. Two aspects are critical for supporting VSD: a) enabling stakeholder inclusion and collaboration in order to elicit and understand their values [6,7], and b) facilitating the education of toolkit users in order to promote self-reflexivity and responsible decision-making [8,5,9].

This paper focuses on the practical application of VSD in RAI toolkits through two Research Questions (RQs):

- • RQ 1: How closely do Value Sensitive Design (VSD) values align with Responsible AI (RAI) values?

- • RQ 2: How do existing RAI toolkits incorporate VSD, and support collaboration and learning?

To address these questions, we conducted an empirical investigation through workshops with 17 participants (AI researchers) (§ 3). The workshops focused on how VSD values are expressed within RAI toolkits, and on the impact of toolkit design features on participants' perceptions of stakeholder collaboration and learning.

The contributions of this study are threefold: (i) mapping VSD values onto commonly used RAI values integrated into the toolkits, which revealed a high degree of alignment between the two sets of values, evidenced by consensus among workshop participants (§ 4.1); (ii) identifying key links between design features in RAI toolkits and their impact on promoting VSD, including navigation methods supporting iteration, open-ended cuing supporting collaboration versus solo work, examples and case studies providing learning opportunities, and value incorporation reducing cognitive load (§ 4.1); and (iii) formulating six practical design recommendations for enhancing value sensitivity in RAI toolkits (§ 5). Focusing on concrete design features such as supporting actionability and shared knowledge, these recommendations complement recent broader suggestions for the focuses and approaches of RAI toolkits [10].
